title: A picture dropped on the panel sections is refused
goal: Dropping a picture on the right hand panel adds it to the document, but only in the empty space below the last section. Over the Layers, Position and Size or Library sections the panel refuses it, so the same panel answers two different ways depending on how far down you let go.
notes: Found on 2026-09-04 while making the window refuse files it cannot use. Cause: the layers panel puts .onDrop(of: [.text], delegate: SectionDropDelegate) on every CollapsibleSection and .onDrop(of: [.text], delegate: LayerRowDropDelegate) on every row. SwiftUI routes a drag to the innermost drop target under the pointer and does NOT fall through to the window-wide destination behind it, so a picture over a section is refused by a delegate that only understands a section id. Mapped with Scripts/playtest/refused-file-panel-walk.json style steps: refused at window y<=320 with two layers, accepted below. Fix is probably to add [.image, EditorState.photonzType] to those two onDrop type lists and forward a picture to editorState.addImageLayerOrOpen, refusing anything else; decide first whether a picture dropped ON a layer row should insert at that position, which is a UX question worth asking.
acceptance: Dragging a picture over any part of the right hand panel shows the copy pointer
Letting a picture go anywhere on the panel adds it as a layer, the same way the empty space below the sections already does
Dragging a layer row or a section header to reorder still works exactly as before
A scripted walk records a picture accepted over a section and over the empty space below it

log.note: Adversarial review before building: the mock has nothing to say here, this is a plain inconsistency. A first-time user drags a screenshot in and aims at whatever is nearest; the panel flipping between the green plus and the no-entry sign as the pointer slides down it is the whole bug. Shortest version that delivers the value: make every part of the panel give the same answer the chrome already gives. Rejected as scope creep: inserting the picture at the row under the pointer with a drop line, and lighting the panel up while a picture is in the air. Both are in the audit's evaluate list so the user can call them.

Reproduced first with Scripts/playtest/panel-takes-picture-walk.json before touching anything: a picture held at window y=80 (Layers header), y=140 (a layer row), y=300 (Position & Size) and y=780 (Library) was refused; the same picture at y=820, below every section, was taken. The harness prints the destination chain and it is one view deep (_PlatformDraggingDestinationView), which confirms there is no fall-through: SwiftUI gates on the registered type list and never offers the drag to the window behind.

Fix: new Sources/Photonz/FileDrop.swift holds the one reading of a file drag (types to register for, whether it carries something placeable, and taking it). EditorView's WindowFileDrop now defers to it, and both inspector delegates register [.text] + FileDrop.types and answer for files: SectionDropDelegate and LayerRowDropDelegate route on whether an internal drag is in flight (dragging / draggingLayerID), so a header or row drag behaves exactly as before and anything else is either a picture (copy, added as a layer) or refused.

Verified: all four acceptance items by re-running the walk. Picture accepted at y=80, 140, 300 and 820; a text file at y=300 still refused; letting go on a layer row took the layer count from 3 to 4; dragging a row still reorders the stack (tree order changed). Scripts/test.sh green, 2947 tests. refused-file-panel-walk, refused-file-walk, drop-preview-walk and multi-drag-walk all still ok. drop-lands-here-walk fails at its dragTile step, but it fails the same way on stashed changes: the probe's Library shelf is empty, nothing to do with this.

One item could not be run: no playtest step can drag a section header, so 'section header reorder still works' was checked by reading the code (that path is gated on dragging != nil and is byte-for-byte the old behaviour). Said so in the audit.
Note on release: LayersPanel.swift and EditorView.swift are shared, and Next has forked neither, so Next gets this for free. Current gets it too, which is the sanctioned direction.
Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-04-panel-takes-picture.json with two real window captures.
